newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan expresses condolences over dead protester.
newsitem.headline: Japan expresses condolences over dead protester.

text.p: Japan expressed condolences over the death of a Hong Kong protester who drowned after jumping off a boat near disputed islands in East China Sea on Thursday, but stood firm on its claim to the islands.

"From the humanitarian perspective, the Government of Japan made utmost efforts to assist in the situation, and regrets from the heart this outcome," Foreign Ministry spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto said in a statement.
"It's our profound hope that the other seriously injured individual fully recovers as soon as possible, and we strongly hope that this type of incident is never repeated," the statement said.

The death of protest group leader David Chan was the first in an increasingly bitter international dispute over the issue of who owns the desolate chain of uninhabited islands -- Japan, Taiwan or China.
Chan was declared dead early in the afternoon by a Japanese doctor who joined Japanese coast guards who were working on board the Hong Kong ship to resuscitate him.

Officials said Chan and three other men jumped off the Hong Kong vessel, Kien Hwa 2, earlier in the day. One other man, Fong Yu Yuen, was injured and taken to hospital in southern Japan's Okinawa prefecture, where he was being kept on a respirator. The others were rescued unhurt.

"We sincerely tried our best to save (their) lives, despite them being protest boats, and we believe it's important we continue such efforts," the Japanese government's chief spokesman, Seiroku Kajiyama, told a news conference.
However, Kajiyama repeated Japan's claim to the islands and urged involved parties to remain calm.
"I understand they are trying to bring up an issue here, but they should not try to complicate the issue," he said.
"Our country has our position and we will continue to claim our stance," Kajiyama said.
The Hong Kong vessel left what Japan claims as its waters around the disputed islands on Thursday afternoon and headed for Taiwan, carrying Chan's body, maritime officials said.
The chartered vessel from Hong Kong had set sail for the islands on Sunday, and had twice entered what Japan considers its territorial waters.

The activists had vowed to reclaim the islands, known as the Senkakus in Japan and Diaoyus in Chinese, saying they would remove a lighthouse built by Japanese rightists in July and raise the red flag of the People's Republic of China.
